B01C195.summary: Dhrishtadyumna tells his father Drupada how the archer won Krishna, and how the winners took refuge at a potter's house where their mother was waiting. Drupada sends his priest to ask who the strangers are, and Yudhishthira answers that the bride's price was paid fairly, so Drupada has no cause to grieve. A messenger then announces that the wedding feast is ready. The chapter sets up the revelation that the strangers are the Pandavas.

scenes.B01C195S01: Dhrishtadyumna reports the contest and the night at the potter's house, Drupada's priest asks the strangers who they are, and Yudhishthira answers and the feast is announced.

shots.B01C195S01H02: Dhrishtadyumna reports the contest: the archer hits the mark, the rival kings are beaten, and the winners take Krishna to a potter's house where their mother waits.
shots.B01C195S01H03: Drupada, delighted, sends his priest to ask who the strangers are, adding that he had long hoped Arjuna would wed his daughter.
shots.B01C195S01H04: Yudhishthira has the priest honoured with water and offerings, then argues that the bride was won fairly and Drupada should not grieve.
shots.B01C195S01H05: A messenger hurries in to say the wedding feast is ready.

B01C196.summary: A messenger invites the group to the wedding feast, and they ride in golden-lotus chariots to Drupada's palace. Drupada lays out goods of many kinds to judge their caste, and the guests are seated and fed with honour. Their royal bearing and interest in the weapons convince Drupada and his son that they are of royal blood.

scenes.B01C196S01: The invitation comes, the party rides to the palace, and Drupada's display and the meal show the guests' royal bearing to Drupada and his son.

shots.B01C196S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C196S01H02: A messenger invites the group to the wedding feast and says the chariots are ready.
shots.B01C196S01H03: The party rides to the palace, Kunti goes inside, and the guests are seated and fed; while Drupada gathers goods to test their rank, the guests' interest in the weapons persuades Drupada and his son that they are royal.

B01C197.summary: Drupada asks who the strangers are, and Yudhishthira reveals that they are Kshatriya sons of Pandu who escaped the lac house. Drupada is overjoyed, vows to help restore Yudhishthira to his throne, and asks Arjuna to take Krishna's hand. Yudhishthira then insists that Krishna be the wife of all five brothers, which Drupada resists, and the family is left to decide the matter when Vyasa arrives.

scenes.B01C197S01: Drupada asks who they are, Yudhishthira reveals the Pandavas' identity and their escape from Varanavata, and Drupada promises support and asks Arjuna to take Krishna's hand.
scenes.B01C197S02: Yudhishthira proposes that Krishna be shared by all five brothers, Drupada objects, Yudhishthira defends it by his mother's command, and Vyasa arrives as the matter is being discussed.

shots.B01C197S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C197S01H02: Drupada asks cheerfully whether they are Kshatriyas, Brahmanas or gods in disguise, and asks for the plain truth.
shots.B01C197S01H03: Yudhishthira declares that they are Kshatriyas and sons of Pandu, names his brothers, and says Kunti and the twins are waiting nearby.
shots.B01C197S01H04: Drupada, overjoyed, asks how they escaped Varanavata, hears the account, blames Dhritarashtra, and vows to restore Yudhishthira's throne.
shots.B01C197S01H05: Drupada gives the group a home and asks Arjuna to take his daughter's hand in marriage that day.
shots.B01C197S02H01: Drupada offers to give Krishna to Yudhishthira or any brother, and Yudhishthira replies that she must be the common wife of all five, as their mother ordered.
shots.B01C197S02H02: Drupada objects that a man may have many wives but no woman has had many husbands, and Yudhishthira answers that morality is subtle and his mother's command settles it.
shots.B01C197S02H03: Drupada asks Yudhishthira, Kunti and Dhrishtadyumna to settle the matter among themselves and tell him by morning.
shots.B01C197S02H04: Yudhishthira, Kunti and Dhrishtadyumna begin to discuss it, and then Vyasa arrives on his wanderings.

B01C198.summary: Vyasa arrives and is welcomed by all, then asks each person for their view of one woman marrying several men. Drupada and Dhrishtadyumna object on grounds of custom and the Vedas, while Yudhishthira cites old precedents and his mother's command. Kunti fears her word may be untrue, and Vyasa promises to explain the custom privately to Drupada, which sets up his defence of polyandry.

scenes.B01C198S01: Vyasa asks for the company's views; Drupada and Dhrishtadyumna object, and Yudhishthira defends the match with precedent and his mother's command.
scenes.B01C198S02: Kunti voices her worry about untruth, and Vyasa says he will explain the custom only to Drupada, taking him aside to begin.

shots.B01C198S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C198S01H02: Everyone rises to greet Vyasa, and after Drupada asks how one woman can wed many men without sin, Vyasa calls the practice obsolete and asks each man's view.
shots.B01C198S01H03: Drupada says the custom is sinful, contrary to usage and the Vedas, and that he cannot agree to it.
shots.B01C198S01H04: Dhrishtadyumna objects that an elder brother should not approach a younger brother's wife, and he refuses to say Draupadi should be shared.
shots.B01C198S01H05: Yudhishthira cites old precedents, a woman who married seven sages and a tree-born maiden who married ten brothers, and argues that his mother's command makes the match virtuous.
shots.B01C198S02H01: Kunti agrees with Yudhishthira but fears her own words may prove untrue.
shots.B01C198S02H02: Vyasa says the matter is an old and eternal virtue, that Yudhishthira's view is sound, and that he will explain it only to Drupada in private.
shots.B01C198S02H03: Vyasa takes Drupada into a private room while the others wait, and begins to explain why the custom is not sinful.

B01C199.summary: Vyasa tells Drupada a story to explain who the Pandavas really are. Yama stopped killing during a sacrifice, and after Indra is humbled by Mahadeva for his pride, he and four other Indras are sent to be born as men, with the goddess Sri as their common wife. Vyasa then identifies the brothers as those Indras and Draupadi as Sri, and grants Drupada divine sight to see them in their former forms.

scenes.B01C199S01: Vyasa tells the story of Yama's pause in killing, Indra's humbling by Mahadeva, the curse that sends five Indras into the world of men, and the birth of Krishna and Valadeva.
scenes.B01C199S02: Vyasa names the brothers as the former Indras and Draupadi as Sri, grants Drupada divine sight, and tells the story of a maiden who asked Mahadeva for five husbands.

shots.B01C199S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C199S01H02: Vyasa says that when Yama paused killing during a sacrifice, humans multiplied, and the gods went to Prajapati, who said Yama would resume his work later.
shots.B01C199S01H03: Indra sees golden lotuses floating down the Bhagirathi, follows the stream to its source, and finds a weeping woman washing there.
shots.B01C199S01H04: The woman leads Indra to a peak where Mahadeva is playing dice; Indra's pride is punished, and he and four other Indras are cursed to be born as men.
shots.B01C199S01H05: Indra makes a fifth Indra, the five are named, Sri is given as their common wife, and Narayana sends two hairs that become Valadeva and Krishna, while the brothers are the Indras and Arjuna is part of Sakra.
shots.B01C199S02H01: Vyasa explains that the Pandavas are those Indras and Draupadi is Sri, who must be born in an extraordinary way, and grants Drupada spiritual sight.
shots.B01C199S02H02: With this sight Drupada sees the brothers in celestial form, is amazed, and hears Vyasa tell of a maiden who asked Mahadeva for five husbands.
shots.B01C199S02H03: Vyasa applies the story to Drupada's daughter, who was pre-ordained to be the common wife of five husbands, and tells the king to do as he wishes.

B01C200.summary: Drupada accepts the story, saying fate and Mahadeva's decree have settled the matter, and gives his consent. Vyasa names an auspicious day, and the wedding goes ahead with Dhaumya presiding, Yudhishthira going first and the brothers taking Krishna's hand in turn. Drupada sends the couples off with cars, elephants, servants and wealth, and the Pandavas settle in his capital.

scenes.B01C200S01: Drupada accepts Vyasa's account, Vyasa names the day, and the wedding is held with Dhaumya presiding, followed by Drupada's gifts and the Pandavas' settling in Panchala.

shots.B01C200S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C200S01H02: Drupada says he now accepts what the gods have ordained, since fate, not his own acts, has settled the marriage, and gives his consent.
shots.B01C200S01H03: The wedding is held on Vyasa's auspicious day, with Dhaumya lighting the fire, the brothers taking Krishna's hand in turn, and Drupada giving rich gifts; the text also notes a marvel that Krishna regained her maidenhood each day.

B01C201.summary: Drupada is pleased with the alliance and no longer fears even the gods. Kunti blesses Krishna, comparing her to famous wives of gods and heroes, and asks her to bear strong sons and rule as queen. Hari (Krishna) then sends the Pandavas costly gifts, including ornaments, robes, servants, elephants, horses and gold, which Yudhishthira accepts to please Govinda.

scenes.B01C201S01: Drupada's women greet Kunti, Kunti blesses Krishna, and Hari (Krishna) sends the newly married Pandavas a great store of gifts.

shots.B01C201S01H01: Heading: the Vaivahika Parva section continues.
shots.B01C201S01H02: Drupada's household women greet Kunti, and Kunti blesses Krishna, comparing her to famous wives and asking for sons and a royal future.
shots.B01C201S01H03: Hari (Krishna) sends the brothers ornaments, robes, servants, elephants, horses and gold, and Yudhishthira accepts them gladly to please Govinda.

B01C202.summary: Word reaches the kings that Draupadi has married the Pandavas, that Arjuna won her in disguise, and that the brothers are alive after all. Duhsasana and the others return to Hastinapura dejected, and Dhritarashtra, first thinking his son has won her, then praises the Pandavas and their powerful allies. Vidura leaves, and Duryodhana and Karna urge their father to weaken the Pandavas before they overpower the Kauravas.

scenes.B01C202S01: News of the marriage spreads, the kings blame Bhishma and Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana returns dejected, and Vidura tells Dhritarashtra the Pandavas are alive and allied with Drupada.
scenes.B01C202S02: After Vidura leaves, Duryodhana and Karna press Dhritarashtra to act against the Pandavas in private.

shots.B01C202S01H02: Spies report that Draupadi has married the Pandavas, and the kings, who had thought the brothers dead in the lac house, blame Bhishma and Dhritarashtra.
shots.B01C202S01H03: Duryodhana and his company return dejected, and Duhsasana says Arjuna only won by disguising himself as a Brahmana and that fate rules.
shots.B01C202S01H04: Vidura tells Dhritarashtra that the Pandavas are alive and allied with Drupada, but the blind king first thinks his own son has won Draupadi and orders ornaments made for her.
shots.B01C202S01H05: Dhritarashtra says the Pandavas are as dear to him as they were to Pandu, and that an alliance with Drupada is a fine thing.
shots.B01C202S02H01: Vidura tells the king to keep his good sense for a hundred years and goes home; then Duryodhana and Karna come to Dhritarashtra alone, accuse him of favouring his enemies, and urge him to weaken the Pandavas before they swallow the Kauravas.

B01C203.summary: With Vidura gone, Dhritarashtra asks his son Duryodhana and Karna to speak openly about how to undo the Pandavas. Duryodhana lists a string of schemes: sowing discord among the brothers, buying off Drupada, luring them away from Panchala, turning Krishna against them, and having Bhima killed. He argues that time is short, because once the brothers win Drupada's trust they will be beyond reach.

scenes.B01C203S01: Dhritarashtra asks for his son's plans in private, and Duryodhana sets out a list of ways to ruin the Pandavas, ending by asking Karna's opinion.

shots.B01C203S01H01: Heading: the Viduragamana Parva section continues.
shots.B01C203S01H02: Dhritarashtra says he will keep his plans from Vidura and asks his son and Karna to speak now that Vidura has left.
shots.B01C203S01H03: Duryodhana lists his schemes, including sowing discord, bribing Drupada, luring the brothers to Panchala or Hastinapura, turning Krishna against them, and having Bhima killed, then asks Karna for his view.

B01C204.summary: Karna argues that Duryodhana's subtle plans cannot work, because the Pandavas are now grown, allied with Drupada, and bound together by their shared wife, and Krishna will not abandon them. He advises an open attack on Drupada before Krishna's Yadava forces arrive. Dhritarashtra praises his courage but wants the elders' advice, and he calls his ministers together.

scenes.B01C204S01: Karna rejects Duryodhana's subtle plans and urges open war on Drupada, Dhritarashtra praises him but asks the elders to advise, and the king gathers his ministers.

shots.B01C204S01H01: Heading: the Viduragamana Parva section continues.
shots.B01C204S01H02: Karna rejects the subtle plans, argues that the brothers cannot be divided or turned against Krishna, and urges an open attack on Drupada before Krishna's forces gather.
shots.B01C204S01H03: Dhritarashtra praises Karna's courage but asks Bhishma, Drona, Vidura and the others to advise on a course that benefits all.
shots.B01C204S01H04: Dhritarashtra calls his chief ministers together to take counsel.

B01C205.summary: Bhishma, asked for his opinion, says he will never approve of a quarrel with the Pandavas, who are as near to him as the Kauravas are. He argues that a good name is what keeps a man alive, and that the brothers' survival and Purochana's death should ease the king's reputation. He urges Duryodhana to give them half the kingdom.

scenes.B01C205S01: Bhishma opposes any quarrel with the Pandavas, appeals to the king's good name, and urges that half the kingdom be given to them.

shots.B01C205S01H01: Heading: the Viduragamana Parva section continues.
shots.B01C205S01H02: Bhishma opposes any quarrel, urges Dhritarashtra to give the Pandavas half the kingdom, and appeals to the king's good name and the brothers' rightful share.

B01C206.summary: Drona agrees with Bhishma and proposes sending a messenger with gifts to Drupada and the Pandavas, then bringing the brothers back to be installed on the throne. Karna mocks both elders as biased and tells the tale of the Magadha king Amvuvicha, whose minister seized power, to argue that kingship depends on fate. Drona rebukes Karna and warns that the Kurus will be destroyed if the good advice is not followed.

scenes.B01C206S01: Drona backs Bhishma and proposes a diplomatic mission; Karna mocks the elders with a tale about kingship and fate, and Drona rebukes him.

shots.B01C206S01H01: Heading: the Viduragamana Parva section continues.
shots.B01C206S01H02: Drona agrees with Bhishma, proposes a messenger with gifts to Drupada and the Pandavas, and then the brothers' return and their installation on the throne.
shots.B01C206S01H03: Karna accuses Bhishma and Drona of bias and tells the tale of the Magadha king Amvuvicha, whose minister seized power, to argue that kingship depends on fate.
shots.B01C206S01H04: Drona calls Karna wicked for trying to harm the Pandavas and warns that the Kurus will be ruined if his advice is followed.

B01C207.summary: Vidura defends Bhishma and Drona as the king's best advisers and calls Karna's counsel malicious. He says the Pandavas are the king's sons as much as Duryodhana is, and argues that they cannot be beaten given their champions and allies. He urges peace with them and an alliance with Drupada, and warns against the counsel of Duryodhana, Karna and Sakuni.

scenes.B01C207S01: Vidura defends the elders, argues the Pandavas are invincible and rightful heirs, and urges the king to make peace with them and win Drupada as an ally.

shots.B01C207S01H01: Heading: the Viduragamana Parva section continues.
shots.B01C207S01H02: Vidura trusts Bhishma and Drona, argues that the Pandavas cannot be beaten given their allies, urges the king to make peace with them and win Drupada as an ally, and warns against Duryodhana, Karna and Sakuni.

B01C208.summary: Dhritarashtra accepts the elders' counsel, calls the Pandavas his children by ordinance, and orders them brought home with Kunti and Krishna. Vidura travels to Drupada with gifts, embraces the brothers and greets Vasudeva. He then delivers Dhritarashtra's message that the Kurus are glad of the alliance and ask the Pandavas to return to their ancestral kingdom.

scenes.B01C208S01: Dhritarashtra accepts the counsel and sends Vidura to bring the Pandavas home, and Vidura delivers gifts and the request to Drupada.

shots.B01C208S01H01: Heading: the Viduragamana Parva section continues.
shots.B01C208S01H02: Dhritarashtra accepts the counsel, calls the Pandavas his children by ordinance, and orders them brought back with Kunti and Krishna.
shots.B01C208S01H03: Vidura travels to Drupada with gifts, embraces the brothers, greets Vasudeva, and hands over the jewels and wealth the Kauravas sent.
shots.B01C208S01H04: Vidura delivers Dhritarashtra's message to Drupada: the Kurus are glad of the alliance and ask that the Pandavas be allowed to return home with Krishna.

B01C209.summary: Drupada agrees that the Pandavas may return to their ancestral kingdom if they and Rama and Krishna agree, and the brothers enter Hastinapura to a joyful welcome. Dhritarashtra sends them to Khandavaprastha with half the kingdom, where they build the great city of Indraprastha, which draws Brahmanas, merchants and craftsmen. Krishna then goes back to Dwaravati with Rama.

scenes.B01C209S01: Drupada gives his consent on condition that the brothers, Rama and Krishna all agree, and Vasudeva supports their return.
scenes.B01C209S02: The Pandavas enter Hastinapura to a joyful welcome, Dhritarashtra sends them to Khandavaprastha, and they build Indraprastha, which attracts many people.
scenes.B01C209S03: The Pandavas settle at Khandavaprastha, and Krishna returns to Dwaravati with Rama.

shots.B01C209S01H01: Heading: the Viduragamana Parva section continues.
shots.B01C209S01H02: Drupada says he is glad of the alliance, but the brothers should go only if they and Rama and Krishna agree.
shots.B01C209S01H03: Yudhishthira replies that he and his brothers depend on Drupada and will do as he commands.
shots.B01C209S01H04: Vasudeva says the Pandavas should go, but that the decision should rest with Drupada.
shots.B01C209S01H05: Drupada agrees with Vasudeva and says he regards the brothers as dear as Vasudeva does.
shots.B01C209S02H01: The Pandavas travel toward Hastinapura, where Vikarna, Chitrasena, Drona and Kripa are sent out to meet them, and the citizens cheer their return.
shots.B01C209S02H02: The brothers pay their respects to Dhritarashtra and Bhishma and to the others present, then go to their rooms.
shots.B01C209S02H03: Dhritarashtra tells Yudhishthira to take up residence at Khandavaprastha, under Arjuna's protection, and rule half the kingdom.
shots.B01C209S02H04: The brothers leave for Khandavaprastha, choose a site with Dwaipayana's help, and build a walled city with a trench and war machines, which they name Indraprastha.
shots.B01C209S02H05: Brahmanas, merchants and craftsmen come to the new city, which is surrounded by gardens, lakes and pleasure-houses, and the brothers' joy grows.
shots.B01C209S03H01: Because Bhishma and Dhritarashtra treated them well, the Pandavas settle at Khandavaprastha, and Krishna goes back to Dwaravati with Rama.

B01C210.summary: Janamejaya asks how the Pandavas governed their new kingdom and how they avoided quarrels while sharing one wife. Vaisampayana says they ruled Indraprastha in harmony until the sage Narada visited, honoured him, and warned them to make a rule about Draupadi. Narada cites the brothers Sunda and Upasunda, who killed each other over a woman, and Yudhishthira asks for the full story.

scenes.B01C210S01: Janamejaya asks about the Pandavas' conduct, Narada visits and warns them of discord, and Yudhishthira asks for the tale behind the warning.

shots.B01C210S01H02: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did after gaining Indraprastha and how no quarrel arose among brothers sharing one wife.
shots.B01C210S01H03: Narada visits the Pandavas, is honoured, and warns them to make a rule about Draupadi so that no quarrel arises, citing the brothers Sunda and Upasunda who killed each other.
shots.B01C210S01H04: Yudhishthira asks Narada who Sunda and Upasunda were, where the quarrel came from, and who Tilottama was, and asks for the full story.

B01C211.summary: Narada tells the story of the Daitya brothers Sunda and Upasunda, sons of Nikumbha, who were inseparable. Through harsh penance in the Vindhya mountains they resist the gods' temptations and illusions, and Brahma refuses them immortality. He grants them invulnerability except from each other, and the brothers return home to a life of revelry.

scenes.B01C211S01: Narada recounts the brothers' birth, their penance on the Vindhya mountains, the gods' attempts to break them, and Brahma's boon that only each other can slay them.

shots.B01C211S01H01: Heading: the Rajya-labha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C211S01H02: The brothers, sons of Nikumbha, perform harsh penance on the Vindhya mountains, resist the gods' temptations and illusions, and win Brahma's favour, though he refuses them immortality.
shots.B01C211S01H03: Brahma grants them invulnerability to all beings except each other, and the brothers return home, where they and their people give themselves to feasting and merriment.

B01C212.summary: Sunda and Upasunda set out with a great army to conquer the three worlds. They overrun heaven and the lower worlds, then turn on the Brahmanas and sacrificers, killing them and destroying sacred sites until ritual and life grind to a halt. They finally settle at Kurukshetra, without a rival.

scenes.B01C212S01: The brothers conquer heaven and the lower worlds, then order the slaughter of sacrificers and Brahmanas, which ruins religion and daily life on earth.

shots.B01C212S01H01: Heading: the Rajya-labha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C212S01H02: The brothers set out with a great army, conquer heaven and the lower worlds, order the killing of sacrificers and Brahmanas, and finally settle at Kurukshetra as the earth falls into ruin.

B01C213.summary: Distressed by the slaughter, the gods and Rishis go to Brahma, who has Viswakarman create a captivating maiden, Tilottama, and send her to make the brothers quarrel over her. As she walks round the assembly, every eye turns to her, and Mahadeva grows extra faces and eyes to watch her. She departs for the Asuras' city, and the great god First Cause dismisses the gathering.

scenes.B01C213S01: The gods appeal to Brahma, Viswakarman creates Tilottama, she walks round the assembly, and then leaves to tempt the brothers.

shots.B01C213S01H01: Heading: the Rajya-labha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C213S01H02: The grieved gods and Rishis approach Brahma, who has Viswakarman create the maiden Tilottama and send her to make the brothers quarrel over her.
shots.B01C213S01H03: Tilottama walks round the assembly, Mahadeva grows four faces and a thousand eyes to watch her, and after she leaves for the Asuras, the great god First Cause dismisses the gathering.

B01C214.summary: Narada tells how the Asura brothers, having conquered everything, grew idle and indulged in pleasure. On the Vindhya plateau both claim the apsara-like Tilottama, fight, and kill each other with their maces. Narada urges the Pandavas to make a rule about Draupadi, and they agree that whoever finds a brother with her must spend twelve years as a celibate forest-dweller.

scenes.B01C214S01: Narada tells how the brothers fell out over Tilottama and destroyed each other, and the Pandavas make a rule about Draupadi on his advice.

shots.B01C214S01H01: Heading: the Rajya-labha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C214S01H02: Having conquered all rivals, the brothers grow idle and indulge in pleasure on a Vindhya plateau, where women dance and sing in their praise.
shots.B01C214S01H03: Tilottama appears, both brothers lust after her and claim her, they fight with their maces and kill each other, and Brahma grants her a boon.
shots.B01C214S01H04: Narada tells the Pandavas that the Asuras destroyed each other over a woman, and asks them to arrange matters so they do not quarrel over Draupadi.
shots.B01C214S01H05: The Pandavas agree on a rule that a brother who sees another with Draupadi must live as a celibate forest-dweller for twelve years, and Narada departs.

B01C215.summary: The Pandavas rule well, and Draupadi delights in her five husbands. When robbers steal a Brahmana's cattle, Arjuna must enter the chamber where Yudhishthira is with Draupadi to fetch his weapons, which breaks the rule the brothers made. Yudhishthira says no fault attaches to a younger brother's entry, but Arjuna insists on keeping his vow and leaves for twelve years in the forest.

scenes.B01C215S01: Arjuna breaks the rule to recover a Brahmana's cattle, Yudhishthira tells him he has no fault, and Arjuna insists on exile to keep his word.
scenes.B01C215S02: Arjuna obtains Yudhishthira's leave and sets out for the forest for twelve years.

shots.B01C215S01H02: The Pandavas rule well, bring many kings under their sway, and Draupadi delights in her five husbands, so the Kuru race prospers.
shots.B01C215S01H03: Robbers steal a Brahmana's cattle, and the weeping Brahmana appeals to the Pandavas to protect his wealth.
shots.B01C215S01H04: Arjuna resolves to act, enters the chamber where Yudhishthira is with Draupadi, recovers the cattle, then asks leave for exile; Yudhishthira says a younger brother's entry is no fault.
shots.B01C215S01H05: Arjuna answers that he cannot waver from truth, which is his weapon.
shots.B01C215S02H01: With the king's permission, Arjuna prepares for forest life and sets out for twelve years.

B01C216.summary: Arjuna sets out for the forest, followed for a distance by Brahmanas, ascetics and musicians. He journeys through forests, rivers and seas, admiring the scenery. At the source of the Ganga he decides to settle.

scenes.B01C216S01: Arjuna leaves for the forest with a retinue of Brahmanas and ascetics and reaches the source of the Ganga, where he thinks of settling.

shots.B01C216S01H01: Heading: the Arjuna-vanavasa Parva section continues.
shots.B01C216S01H02: Brahmanas and ascetics follow Arjuna for a distance, he journeys like Indra with the Maruts, and at the source of the Ganga he decides to stay.

B01C217.summary: At the source of the Ganga, the Naga princess Ulupi drags Arjuna into the river and into her palace, and he agrees to yield to her in spite of his vow. She grants him invincibility in water. Arjuna then visits holy sites across the north, east and coast, and at Manipura he marries Chitrangada, daughter of King Chitravahana, whose son is to carry on the royal line.

scenes.B01C217S01: At the Ganga's source, Ulupi pulls Arjuna into her Naga palace, persuades him to yield, and grants him invincibility in water.
scenes.B01C217S02: Arjuna visits holy sites, reaches Manipura, and marries Chitrangada on her father's terms, then goes on his way after she bears a son.

shots.B01C217S01H01: At the Ganga's source, Ulupi, daughter of the Naga king Kauravya, pulls Arjuna into the water and into her palace, and he asks who she is.
shots.B01C217S01H02: Ulupi says she is Kauravya's daughter, overcome by desire for him, and asks him to yield to her.
shots.B01C217S01H03: Arjuna replies that his twelve-year vow binds him and asks how he can please her without breaking truth or duty.
shots.B01C217S01H04: Ulupi argues that the rule only concerns the brothers' shared wife, that helping the distressed is virtuous, and that she will destroy herself if refused.
shots.B01C217S01H05: Arjuna yields, spends the night in her palace, returns in the morning, and Ulupi grants him invincibility in water.
shots.B01C217S02H03: Arjuna tells the Brahmanas what happened, visits holy peaks and waters, and at Manipura is given Chitrangada by King Chitravahana on terms that her son continue the line; after she bears a son, Arjuna goes on his way.

B01C218.summary: Arjuna goes to the sacred waters on the southern ocean, which the ascetics shun because crocodiles lurk there and seize bathers. He bathes in the Saubhadra water, is seized by a crocodile, and drags it ashore. The crocodile turns into the Apsara Varga, who begins to explain that she and her companions were cursed after tempting a Brahmana.

scenes.B01C218S01: Arjuna visits the shunned sacred waters, wrestles a crocodile at Saubhadra, and the freed Apsara begins to explain her curse.

shots.B01C218S01H01: Heading: the Arjuna-vanavasa Parva section continues.
shots.B01C218S01H02: Arjuna visits five sacred waters on the southern ocean, finds them shunned, and asks the ascetics why, and they say crocodiles seize bathers there.
shots.B01C218S01H03: Arjuna plunges into the Saubhadra water, drags a seizing crocodile ashore, and it becomes the Apsara Varga, who begins to explain how she and her companions were cursed after tempting a Brahmana.

B01C219.summary: Varga explains that the Brahmana pardoned her and her companions but fixed their punishment at a hundred years, after which a worthy man would free them, and that the waters would be called Nari-tirthas. Narada told them to seek Arjuna at the southern waters, and Arjuna frees all the Apsaras. He then returns to Manipura to see Chitrangada and their son Vabhruvahana, before going on to Gokarna.

scenes.B01C219S01: Varga recounts the Brahmana's curse and pardon and Narada's advice, Arjuna frees the Apsaras, and he visits Chitrangada and his son before moving on to Gokarna.

shots.B01C219S01H01: Heading: the Arjuna-vanavasa Parva section continues.
shots.B01C219S01H02: Varga and her companions beg the Brahmana to pardon them, arguing that women should not be slain and that a Brahmana should protect those who seek shelter.
shots.B01C219S01H03: The Brahmana relents, but says they will be crocodiles for a hundred years until a worthy man frees them, and that the waters will be called Nari-tirthas.
shots.B01C219S01H04: Varga says Narada sent them to the five southern waters, where Arjuna would free them, and she asks him to help her companions as well.
shots.B01C219S01H05: Arjuna frees all the Apsaras, who regain their own forms, then visits Chitrangada and his son Vabhruvahana at Manipura and goes on to Gokarna.

B01C220.summary: Arjuna tours the sacred places on the western shore and reaches Prabhasa, where Krishna comes to meet him. The two friends talk, feast and enjoy entertainments on Raivataka mountain, and then ride in a golden car to Dwaraka. The Yadava city turns out to welcome Arjuna, who takes up residence with Krishna.

scenes.B01C220S01: Arjuna tours the western holy places, meets Krishna at Prabhasa and on Raivataka, and is welcomed into Dwaraka, where he stays with Krishna.

shots.B01C220S01H01: Heading: the Arjuna-vanavasa Parva section continues.
shots.B01C220S01H02: Arjuna tours the western holy places, meets Krishna at Prabhasa and on Raivataka, and is welcomed into Dwaraka, where the two friends stay together for many days.

B01C221.summary: A grand festival of the Vrishnis and Andhakas begins on Raivataka, with Haladhara (Valarama), Ugrasena, Satyaki and many others in attendance. Arjuna sees Bhadra, Vasudeva's daughter and Krishna's sister, and asks Krishna to help him win her. Krishna's side suggests carrying her off by force, which is praised for brave Kshatriyas, and messengers are sent to Yudhishthira, who consents.

scenes.B01C221S01: The Raivataka festival opens, Arjuna sees Bhadra and asks Krishna for her hand, and the plan to carry her off with Yudhishthira's assent is set.

shots.B01C221S01H02: A grand festival of the Vrishnis and Andhakas begins on Raivataka, with gifts to Brahmanas, music, dancing, and the presence of many heroes including Haladhara (Valarama).
shots.B01C221S01H03: Arjuna sees Bhadra, Krishna's sister, is struck with desire, and Krishna offers to speak to their father if Arjuna is serious.
shots.B01C221S01H04: Arjuna asks for her hand; the reply, attributed to Vasudeva, says a self-choice is doubtful, so abduction is praised for brave warriors, and messengers carry the plan to Yudhishthira, who consents.

B01C222.summary: Arjuna, with Krishna's assent, drives off in his golden car with Subhadra, and her attendants flee to Dwaraka to raise the alarm. The Vrishnis and Andhakas arm in anger, and Valadeva, wine-flushed, first tells them to wait for Krishna's word, then rages at Arjuna and vows to make the earth empty of Kauravas. The assembly roars its approval.

scenes.B01C222S01: Arjuna carries off Subhadra, the Yadava court sounds the alarm, and Valadeva rages at the insult while the others await Krishna's word.

shots.B01C222S01H01: Heading: the Subhadra-harana Parva section continues.
shots.B01C222S01H02: Arjuna, with Krishna's assent, seizes Subhadra on her way back from Raivataka and drives toward Indraprastha, while her attendants flee to Dwaraka and the court sounds the alarm and the warriors arm.
shots.B01C222S01H03: Valadeva, wine-flushed, first tells the warriors to wait for Krishna's word, then rages at Arjuna's insult and vows to make the earth empty of Kauravas, and the assembly roars its approval.

B01C223.summary: Vasudeva defends Arjuna's abduction of Subhadra as a proper form of marriage for a warrior, and the Vrishnis are persuaded to bring Arjuna back for a lawful wedding. Krishna and Balarama then come to Indraprastha with rich gifts, and Subhadra bears the son Abhimanyu. Draupadi bears five sons, one to each brother, and all are trained in arms by Arjuna and Dhaumya.

scenes.B01C223S01: Vasudeva defends the abduction, Arjuna marries Subhadra, the Vrishnis bring gifts to Indraprastha, and Abhimanyu and Draupadi's five sons are born and trained.

shots.B01C223S01H02: Persuaded by Vasudeva, the Vrishnis bring Arjuna back to Dwaraka for a lawful marriage, and later Draupadi's jealousy fades when the new bride Subhadra humbly greets her.
shots.B01C223S01H03: Krishna comes to Indraprastha with a great Vrishni host, Yudhishthira honours them, and Krishna and Rama load the Pandavas with gifts before the visitors return home; Subhadra then bears Abhimanyu.
shots.B01C223S01H04: Abhimanyu grows into a skilled warrior, and Draupadi bears five sons, Prativindhya, Sutasoma, Srutakarman, Satanika and Srutasena, who are educated by Dhaumya.

B01C224.summary: Yudhishthira rules Indraprastha so justly that his subjects, his brothers and other kings prosper in virtue. Arjuna proposes a summer outing on the Yamuna, and he and Krishna go with friends to a pleasant grove for feasting and revelry. While the two heroes talk apart, a radiant Brahmana approaches, and they rise to receive him.

scenes.B01C224S01: Yudhishthira's prosperous rule is described, Arjuna and Krishna set out for a summer outing on the Yamuna, and a radiant Brahmana approaches them as they talk.

shots.B01C224S01H02: Yudhishthira rules Indraprastha so justly that his subjects, brothers and other kings prosper, and the people love him for his fairness and affection.
shots.B01C224S01H03: After some days, Arjuna proposes a summer outing on the banks of the Yamuna, and Vasudeva agrees.
shots.B01C224S01H04: With Yudhishthira's leave, Arjuna and Krishna go with friends to a pleasant grove, where the women and company drink, dance, sing and play.
shots.B01C224S01H05: Arjuna and Krishna sit apart and talk of past deeds, and when a radiant Brahmana approaches they rise and wait for his commands.

B01C225.summary: Agni, in the guise of a hungry Brahmana, asks Arjuna and Krishna to help him burn the Khandava forest, which Indra protects because it shelters his friend, the Naga Takshaka. Vaisampayana then tells the story of King Swetaki, whose priests grew weary of his endless sacrifices and left him, and who won Rudra's help after a long penance. Agni fell ill from the butter he drank at that sacrifice, and he must now eat the creatures of Khandava to recover, but the forest's inhabitants put out his fire again and again.

scenes.B01C225S01: Agni asks Arjuna and Krishna to help him burn Khandava, and the narrator tells the story of King Swetaki, whose sacrifice ended up making Agni sick.
scenes.B01C225S02: Agni, surfeited from twelve years of butter, is told by the Creator to eat the forest's creatures, but the forest dwellers repeatedly put his blaze out.

shots.B01C225S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C225S01H02: Agni, in the guise of a Brahmana, asks Arjuna and Krishna to help him burn Khandava, which Indra protects for his friend Takshaka, by holding back the rain and stopping any escape.
shots.B01C225S01H03: Janamejaya asks why Agni wants to burn the forest full of creatures and asks for the full story.
shots.B01C225S01H04: Vaisampayana tells how King Swetaki, abandoned by his weary priests, won Rudra's help after a long penance and twelve years of offerings, and Rudra sent Durvasa to officiate.
shots.B01C225S01H05: A closing line: King Swetaki's story ends with his ascent to heaven, accompanied by the priests who served him.
shots.B01C225S02H01: Agni, sick from the butter of Swetaki's sacrifice, is told by the Creator to eat the forest's creatures, but the dwellers of the forest put his fire out seven times.

B01C226.summary: Agni, still ill and frustrated, goes to Brahma, who explains that Arjuna and Vasudeva are the incarnations of the ancient gods Nara and Narayana, and points Agni to them for help. Agni asks them to aid him. Arjuna replies that he needs a worthy bow, inexhaustible quivers and a fitting car to hold back Indra's rain.

scenes.B01C226S01: Brahma sends Agni to Arjuna and Vasudeva, and Arjuna lists the weapons he needs for the task.

shots.B01C226S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C226S01H02: Brahma tells Agni that Arjuna and Vasudeva are Nara and Narayana, so Agni goes to them for help, and Arjuna asks for a bow, quivers and a car, plus the means to thwart Indra's rain.

B01C227.summary: Agni calls on Varuna, who gives Arjuna the bow Gandiva, two inexhaustible quivers and a car with an ape banner drawn by white steeds. Agni gives Krishna a fiery discus, and Varuna adds a mace called Kaumodaki. Armed, the two heroes promise to help Agni, who then surrounds the forest with his flames.

scenes.B01C227S01: Agni summons Varuna, Arjuna and Krishna receive celestial weapons and a car, and Agni blazes around the forest.

shots.B01C227S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C227S01H02: Varuna gives Arjuna the bow Gandiva, two quivers and a car, Agni gives Krishna a discus, Varuna adds a mace, and the two heroes promise to help Agni.
shots.B01C227S01H03: Agni surrounds the forest with his seven flames and burns it with a roar that makes every creature tremble.

B01C228.summary: Arjuna and Krishna take positions on opposite sides of the forest and cut down creatures trying to escape, while the fire kills others in agony. The gods go to Indra and ask whether the end of the world has come. Indra covers the sky with clouds, but the heat of the fire dries up the rain until he gathers a heavier downpour.

scenes.B01C228S01: Arjuna and Krishna cut down creatures fleeing the burning forest, the gods appeal to Indra, and Indra's rain struggles against the fire.

shots.B01C228S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C228S01H02: Arjuna and Krishna take up opposite sides of the forest and cut down fleeing creatures while the others perish in the flames, and the gods go to Indra to ask whether the world is ending.
shots.B01C228S01H03: Indra covers the sky with clouds to protect Khandava, but the heat dries his showers, so he gathers heavier clouds and the forest fills with smoke and lightning.

B01C229.summary: Arjuna blocks Indra's rain with a storm of arrows and his Vayavya weapon while Agni blazes on. When the young Naga Aswasena tries to escape by being swallowed by his mother, Arjuna beheads her, but Indra's wind stuns Arjuna and Aswasena gets away. The gods then join the battle with their weapons, and Arjuna and Krishna repel them, with Arjuna shattering a mountain-peak that Indra hurls at him.

scenes.B01C229S01: Arjuna blocks Indra's rain, Aswasena escapes, and the gods join the fight, which Arjuna and Krishna win before Indra's mountain is shattered.

shots.B01C229S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C229S01H02: Arjuna blocks Indra's rain and beheads the Naga mother who tries to swallow her son Aswasena, but Indra's wind stuns Arjuna and Aswasena escapes; then the gods, including Yama, Kuvera, Skanda and Varuna, join the battle and are beaten back, and Arjuna shatters the mountain-peak Indra hurls at him.

B01C231.summary: Janamejaya asks why the Sarngaka birds survived the fire, and Vaisampayana tells how the ascetic Mandapala, refused entry to the realm of the Pitris for want of children, took the form of a Sarngaka and fathered four sons. When he saw Agni coming to burn Khandava, he praised the god at length and asked him to spare his unhatched sons. Agni agreed.

scenes.B01C231S01: Janamejaya asks why the birds survived, and Vaisampayana tells how Mandapala, denied heaven, fathered sons as a bird and then praised Agni.
scenes.B01C231S02: Agni, pleased with the praise, agrees to spare Mandapala's sons while burning the forest.

shots.B01C231S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C231S01H02: Janamejaya asks why Agni did not burn the Sarngaka birds and asks for the reason.
shots.B01C231S01H03: Vaisampayana tells of the learned and austere ascetic Mandapala, who on reaching the realm of the Pitris finds that he is refused the expected reward.
shots.B01C231S01H04: The celestials tell him that men are born in debt, that children discharge it, and that his lack of offspring is why heaven is closed to him, so he should beget children.
shots.B01C231S01H05: Mandapala takes the form of a Sarngaka, fathers four Vedic sons with the bird Jarita, then leaves them in the forest and goes to another wife, and when he sees Agni coming to burn Khandava he praises the god at length.
shots.B01C231S02H01: Pleased by the praise, Agni asks what boon he can grant, and Mandapala asks him to spare his children while burning the forest, which Agni agrees to do.

B01C232.summary: As the fire closes in, the mother bird Jarita weeps, unable to save all of her unfledged chicks. Her young urge her to save herself, since she can have other children, and she suggests hiding them in a mouse's hole until the fire passes. The chicks refuse, arguing that being eaten by the mouse would be more shameful than dying in the fire.

scenes.B01C232S01: The fire approaches, Jarita laments, her chicks urge her to save herself, she proposes a mouse's hole, and the chicks refuse.

shots.B01C232S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C232S01H02: As the fire approaches, the helpless mother Jarita weeps, unable to save all her chicks, and asks herself what she should do.
shots.B01C232S01H03: The chicks tell their mother to save herself, since she can bear more children while their deaths would end the line.
shots.B01C232S01H04: Jarita suggests the chicks hide in a mouse's hole and that she will cover its mouth with dust until the fire has passed.
shots.B01C232S01H05: The chicks refuse, arguing that without feathers they would be eaten by the mouse, and that death by fire is more honourable than being devoured.

B01C230.summary: Krishna's discus and Arjuna's arrows cut down the creatures of Khandava, and the gods retreat after an unseen voice tells Indra that Arjuna and Vasudeva are Nara and Narayana and that the forest's fate is sealed. Krishna and Arjuna spare the Asura Maya when he runs to Arjuna for protection, and Agni burns the forest for many days. Only six creatures survive: Aswasena, Maya and four Sarngaka birds.

scenes.B01C230S01: The creatures of Khandava are slaughtered as the gods retreat, Arjuna shields the Asura Maya from Agni, and Agni burns the forest for many days.
scenes.B01C230S02: Agni spares six of the forest's dwellers, named as Aswasena, Maya and four birds.

shots.B01C230S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C230S01H02: The creatures of Khandava flee in terror, Krishna's discus and Arjuna's arrows cut them down, and an unseen voice tells Indra that the two heroes are Nara and Narayana and that Khandava's destruction is fated, so the gods withdraw.
shots.B01C230S01H03: Krishna sees the Asura Maya escaping, Agni pursues him, and Maya begs Arjuna for protection, which Arjuna grants.
shots.B01C230S01H04: Protected from Indra by Krishna and Arjuna, Agni sets about burning the forest in earnest.
shots.B01C230S01H05: Agni burns the forest for five and ten days, gorging on the fat and flesh of its creatures.
shots.B01C230S02H01: Agni spares only six of the forest's dwellers.
shots.B01C230S02H02: The six survivors are named as Aswasena, Maya and four birds called Sarngakas.

B01C233.summary: Jarita tells her sons that a hawk has carried off the mouse, so the hole is now safe. The chicks doubt her, pointing out that other mice may remain, and urge her to save herself so she can have other children. She insists she saw the hawk take the mouse, but they still refuse, and she leaves them as the fire closes in.

scenes.B01C233S01: Jarita insists the hole is safe, the chicks refuse and urge her to save herself, and she leaves them as the fire approaches.

shots.B01C233S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C233S01H02: Jarita says a hawk has seized the mouse, so the hole is safe, but the chicks reply that other mice may remain and urge their mother to save herself.
shots.B01C233S01H03: Jarita insists she saw the hawk carry the mouse off and urges them to enter, but the chicks still refuse and tell her to go and find another husband.
shots.B01C233S01H04: Jarita leaves her sons in the forest and goes to a place without fire, and Agni rushes toward the chicks, and the eldest, Jaritari, begins to speak to the god.

B01C234.summary: The four sons of Mandapala speak their last words before the fire reaches them. Jaritari says the wise remain awake facing death, and the others speak of the eldest's duty to protect them and of the fire's threat. Each then sings a hymn of praise to Agni, asking the god to spare them, and Agni agrees to do so, remembering his promise to their father.

scenes.B01C234S01: The four brothers speak in turn about wisdom, the eldest's duty, and the approaching fire.
scenes.B01C234S02: Each brother sings a hymn of praise to Agni and asks for protection.
scenes.B01C234S03: Agni, mindful of his promise to Mandapala, agrees to spare the birds, and Drona asks him to consume the creatures that trouble them.

shots.B01C234S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C234S01H02: Jaritari says the wise remain awake facing death and feel no pangs, while the confused suffer and gain no salvation.
shots.B01C234S01H03: Sarisrikka praises his eldest brother's patience and wisdom, noting that only one among many is wise and brave.
shots.B01C234S01H04: Stamvamitra says the eldest is the protector, and if he cannot save them the younger brothers can do nothing.
shots.B01C234S01H05: Drona warns that the seven-tongued fire of the god is quickly approaching their home.
shots.B01C234S02H01: Vaisampayana introduces the four hymns that each son addresses to Agni.
shots.B01C234S02H02: Jaritari's hymn calls Agni the soul of air and the body of vegetation, with flames stretching in every direction.
shots.B01C234S02H03: Sarisrikka's hymn describes the brothers' orphaned state and feathers not yet grown, and begs Agni for protection by another route.
shots.B01C234S02H04: Stamvamitra's hymn calls Agni the all-in-one, the sustainer of creatures, and the one who both creates and destroys the universe.
shots.B01C234S02H05: Drona's hymn praises Agni as the digester of food and the sun that draws up water as rain, and asks him to spare them by going another way.
shots.B01C234S03H01: Pleased, and recalling his promise to Mandapala, Agni calls Drona a Rishi and says he will do as they ask.
shots.B01C234S03H02: Drona asks Agni to consume the cats that trouble them every day, along with their friends and relatives.
shots.B01C234S03H03: Agni agrees, tells the Sarngakas his intentions, and begins to burn the forest of Khandava with greater strength.

B01C235.summary: Mandapala frets about his sons, and his second wife Lapita answers jealously that he cares more for her rival Jarita. Mandapala replies that he sought children for their sake and leaves Lapita to go her own way. When he reaches the sons, they greet him coldly, and Jarita quarrels with him over Lapita, until he cites the story of Arundhati and the sons finally come forward to worship him.

scenes.B01C235S01: Mandapala worries aloud to Lapita, the two quarrel over his divided attention, and he finds his sons safe but cold toward him.
scenes.B01C235S02: Mandapala and Jarita quarrel, he cites Arundhati's jealousy, and the sons finally come forward to greet and worship him.

shots.B01C235S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C235S01H02: Mandapala worries aloud to his second wife Lapita about his sons' safety and the danger from the fire and wind.
shots.B01C235S01H03: Lapita answers jealously that Agni has promised to save them, and accuses Mandapala of caring more for his rival Jarita.
shots.B01C235S01H04: Mandapala replies that he sought children for their sake, that abandoning what he has is wicked, and that Lapita may do as she chooses.
shots.B01C235S01H05: Jarita finds her children safe and embraces them, but when Mandapala arrives his sons greet him coldly and neither they nor Jarita speak kindly to him.
shots.B01C235S02H01: Mandapala asks which child is the eldest and why no one answers him, saying he left them but was unhappy elsewhere.
shots.B01C235S02H02: Jarita tells him to return to Lapita, and Mandapala argues that co-wives and lovers ruin women's happiness, citing Arundhati's jealousy of Vasishtha.
shots.B01C235S02H03: The sons come forward to worship their father, and he gives them every assurance.

B01C236.summary: Mandapala tells his sons that he delayed out of trust in Agni's promise and in their own strength, and asks them to bear no resentment. Agni, having consumed Khandava with Krishna and Arjuna's help and drunk its fat and marrow, shows himself to Arjuna, and Indra offers the heroes boons. Arjuna asks for Indra's weapons and Krishna asks for eternal friendship, and the three then rest on a riverbank.

scenes.B01C236S01: Mandapala reassures his sons, Agni is satisfied, Indra grants boons to Arjuna and Krishna, and Arjuna, Krishna and Maya rest by a river.
scenes.B01C236S02: The Adi Parva closes, followed by a licence notice from the Project Gutenberg edition.

shots.B01C236S01H01: Heading: the Khandava-daha Parva section continues.
shots.B01C236S01H02: Mandapala tells his sons that he had Agni's promise and delayed out of trust, and asks them to bear no resentment, since they are all learned Rishis.
shots.B01C236S01H03: Mandapala takes his wife and sons and leaves the region for another country.
shots.B01C236S01H04: Agni, having consumed the forest with Krishna and Arjuna's help, shows himself to Arjuna, and Indra, surrounded by the Maruts, descends to offer each of them a boon.
shots.B01C236S01H05: Arjuna asks for Indra's weapons, Krishna asks for an eternal friendship, and Agni lets the heroes go wherever they choose, after which Arjuna, Krishna and Maya sit down by a river.
shots.B01C236S02H01: Heading: the end of the Adi Parva.
shots.B01C236S02H02: Boilerplate from the Project Gutenberg licence, not part of the epic text.
